title: FOMC minutes of the Dec 7-8, 2027 meeting (the year's final SEP) — D+21 by the Board's own record, but the least safe D+21 extrapolation this family has made
source: EST: derived this session 2026-09-08 from the Board's own release record rather than from a published minutes calendar, which does not exist for 2027. All 45 '(Released ...)' strings on federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm (HTTP 200, 164,831 bytes, page stamp 'Last Update: August 19, 2026') were parsed and paired to their meetings PANEL BY PANEL -- a global regex crosses panel boundaries and yields phantom pairs, the trap fomc-2027-09-15 banked. The lag histogram is D+21 x 42, D+20 x 2, D+19 x 1, so the modal and near-universal rule is minutes at D+21 from the decision day, always a Wednesday. 2027-12-08 is a Wednesday and 2027-12-08 + 21 days = Wednesday 2027-12-29. THE DECEMBER-SPECIFIC CUT IS WHY THIS IS FILED WITH A WARNING RATHER THAN AS ROUTINE ARITHMETIC, and it is new to this family: four of the five December meetings in the record released at exactly D+21 Wednesday -- 2021-12-15 -> 2022-01-05, 2022-12-14 -> 2023-01-04, 2023-12-13 -> 2024-01-03, 2024-12-18 -> 2025-01-08 -- and ALL FOUR LANDED IN JANUARY of the following year. The single exception is the one December meeting early enough for D+21 to fall inside the Christmas-New Year window: 2025-12-10, whose D+21 would have been Friday 2025-12-31, and whose minutes were instead PULLED FORWARD to Tuesday 2025-12-30 (D+20). 2027-12-08 + 21 = 2027-12-29 sits squarely inside that same window, a placement with NO PRECEDENT among the five -- no December meeting in the record has released its minutes on December 29. So this date carries the rule's answer AND the explicit flag that this is precisely the configuration that displaced the only December exception; a pull-forward to Tue 2027-12-28 or a push to a January 2028 date are both live. The 14:00 ET release time is the standing convention and is not on this page. Discovered during the fomc-2027-12-08 initial research, checked 2026-09-08
notes: PROPOSED by the fomc-2027-12-08 initial research (2026-09-08). Its +/-5-day corridor (2027-12-03 to 2027-12-13) returned ZERO tracked events for a high-impact decision, and this calendar carries no minutes entry for any 2027 meeting after fomc-minutes-2027-10-06. THIS ENTRY IS FILED WITH AN UNUSUALLY LOUD CAVEAT AND THE PROPOSER WANTS IT READ: the D+21 rule holds 42 of 45 times overall and 4 of 5 times for December, but every one of those four December instances released into JANUARY, and the lone exception is the only one whose D+21 fell in the Christmas-New Year window -- 2025-12-10, pulled forward from Fri 2025-12-31 to Tue 2025-12-30. 2027-12-29 is in that window. Whoever researches this id should treat the date as the rule's best answer under a KNOWN displacement risk, not as settled arithmetic, and should re-check it against the Board's published 2027 release schedule once one exists; the sensible falsifier is a release on Tue 2027-12-28 or on a January 2028 date. This sharpens rather than contradicts fomc-2027-09-15 leg 12, which recorded the same three exceptions and characterised them generally as 'a late-year release pulled off a holiday week' -- the December-only cut above is what makes the risk specific to THIS date rather than generic. WHAT THIS MEETING'S MINUTES CARRY, for whoever picks it up: the Dec 7-8 2027 meeting is the year's final one and publishes the year's final SEP, the first to carry the 2028 dot path, so its minutes are the first narrative account of how that path was set. The proposer tested and REFUTED the obvious volatility inference from that structure -- SEP-month decision days (n=77) run 0.989% against non-SEP (n=79) 0.862%, permutation P = 0.405, and June is a SEP meeting and the QUIETEST cell in the table at 0.522% -- which replicates fomc-2027-09-15 leg 7's independent null on the Board's own horizon-extension distinction (0.875 vs 0.696, P = 0.144). Two sessions have now failed to find a volatility signature in SEP structure: it is an attribution fact about what a meeting publishes, not a base rate. AND THE BASE-RATE TABLE ITSELF IS RETIRED by the proposing lane -- selection-corrected, P(max of 12 monthly decision-day cells >= December's 1.265%) = 0.8212, and at the table's true maximum, August's 1.482%, P = 0.4076 -- so no December-specific cell should be quoted for this entry either. IMPACT MEDIUM, matching every other fomc-minutes-* entry in this calendar. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
